Types of Car Accident Claims in Grand Junction, CO
Not every crash is the same, and neither is the claim that follows. The legal path forward is shaped by the circumstances of the accident, who was at fault, and what coverage is available.
Some of the most common claim types our attorneys handle include:
DUI and Impaired Driving
When a driver is impaired by alcohol or drugs, gross negligence findings can support punitive damages in addition to standard compensation.
Distracted and Reckless Driving
Texting, aggressive lane changes, and speeding on corridors like Highway 50 and North Avenue are among the most common causes of serious crashes in Grand Junction.
Rear-End and Intersection Collisions:
Stop-and-go traffic on heavily traveled local routes generates a high volume of rear-impact and right-of-way crashes.
Commercial Vehicle Accidents:
Crashes involving trucks and delivery vehicles on I-70 carry federal regulatory complexity, multiple layers of liability, and some of the highest damage values in personal injury law.
Uninsured and Underinsured Motorist Claims
When the at-fault driver fled the scene or carried insufficient coverage, UM/UIM claims filed against your own policy may be the primary path to compensation.

The sooner an attorney gets involved, the better positioned your case will be. Evidence disappears, witnesses become harder to reach, and insurers move quickly. Getting legal guidance early can make a significant difference in what you may be able to recover.
Common Car Accident Injuries in Grand Junction, CO

Injuries from a car crash do not always make themselves known right away. Some appear at the scene, others surface days later. Regardless of when symptoms develop, getting evaluated promptly protects both your health and your claim.
Common injuries our attorneys see in car accident cases in Grand Junction include:
Whiplash
A rapid back-and-forth movement of the neck that damages muscles, ligaments, and discs. Symptoms often peak days after the crash, according to the
National Library of Medicine
, making early evaluation important even when pain feels minor.
Traumatic Brain Injuries
A forceful blow or jolt to the head can cause anything from temporary cognitive disruption to permanent disability, according to the
National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke
. Even moderate-speed crashes can produce TBI.
Spinal Cord Injuries
Damage to the spinal cord can result in chronic pain, loss of function, or permanent paralysis, depending on the severity and location of the injury.
Broken Bones:
Rib fractures, wrist injuries, and leg breaks are common in side-impact and head-on collisions.
Internal Organ Damage:
Blunt force trauma can injure the liver, spleen, or kidneys without any external signs.
Soft Tissue Injuries:
Damage to muscles, tendons, and ligaments can limit mobility and daily function for months, often with limited visible evidence on early imaging.
Facial and Dental Injuries:
Contact with airbags, steering wheels, or shattered glass can cause lacerations, fractures, and dental injuries.
Medical records tied to the crash date are the foundation of any injury claim. Waiting to seek treatment gives insurers room to argue that your injuries were unrelated to the accident.
What to Do After a Car Accident in Grand Junction
Knowing what injuries are at stake makes the steps that follow even more important. Under

, any driver involved in a crash must stop, remain at the scene, and exchange information with all other parties. Beyond that legal requirement, taking the right steps in the hours following a crash can significantly affect how a claim develops.
Here is what you should do:
Call 911 and request law enforcement. A police report creates an official third-party record insurance adjusters rely on when evaluating fault.
Seek medical attention immediately, even when symptoms feel minor. Delayed treatment creates documentation gaps insurers use to dispute injury severity.
Document the scene with photographs of vehicle positions, road conditions, traffic controls, and visible damage from multiple angles.
Gather witness contact information before people leave the scene. Independent accounts frequently become decisive in disputed liability cases.
Notify your insurance company promptly, but limit details to basic facts. Do not give a recorded statement to any insurer without legal guidance first.
Contact a
Grand Junction car accident lawyer
before speaking further with anyone from the at-fault driver’s insurance company.

Physical evidence disappears quickly. Skid marks fade, surveillance footage gets overwritten, and witnesses become harder to locate. An attorney engaged early can preserve what matters before it is gone.
Compensation You Can Recover in a Car Accident Claim
A car accident can affect every part of your life, from your ability to work to your ability to do the things you once took for granted.
Colorado law allows injured drivers to pursue compensation
across several categories:
Economic damages cover quantifiable financial losses:
Medical expenses, from emergency care through ongoing treatment and rehabilitation
Future treatment costs for injuries requiring long-term or permanent care
Lost wages for time missed from work during recovery
Reduced earning capacity if your injuries prevent you from earning the same income in the future
Property repair or replacement for vehicle damage
Non-economic damages address the personal toll of the crash:
Physical pain and suffering
Emotional distress and anxiety
Loss of enjoyment of life for activities no longer possible due to injury
Inconvenience and disruption to daily life
In cases involving particularly reckless or willful conduct, punitive damages may also be available. When injuries are serious, future losses can represent the largest portion of a claim. At
Dormer Harpring
, we work with medical and economic experts to make sure every dollar of your actual loss is documented before any settlement is considered.
Who Can Be Held Liable for the Car Accident?
Liability in a
Grand Junction car accident
case is not always limited to the other driver. Depending on the circumstances, responsibility may extend to the following:
The at-fault driver, whose negligence caused or contributed to the crash
A trucking company or employer, when the at-fault driver was acting within the scope of their job
A vehicle manufacturer, when a defective part, such as a brake system or tire, contributed to the collision
A government entity, when unsafe road design, failed traffic signals, or inadequate signage on Mesa County roads played a role
A third-party contractor, when negligent maintenance of roadways or vehicles contributed to the crash
Colorado follows a modified comparative negligence rule under

. As long as your share of fault stays below 50 percent, you can still recover compensation, though your damages will be reduced proportionally. Insurers routinely try to shift blame onto injured drivers to lower what they pay out, which is why having a
Grand Junction car accident lawyer
conduct an accurate fault analysis from the start can make a significant difference in your outcome.
Colorado Auto Accident and Insurance Laws
Colorado requires all drivers to carry minimum liability coverage. According to the
Colorado General Assembly
, those minimums as of 2026 are:
$25,000 per person for bodily injury
$50,000 per accident when more than one person is injured
$15,000 for property damage

These figures represent the legal minimum, not a sufficient level of protection. Serious injuries routinely exceed these limits, which is where uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage becomes important. Colorado insurers are required to offer UM/UIM coverage, and when the at-fault driver’s policy falls short, it can become the primary source of compensation.
Colorado is also an at-fault state. Under

, your compensation is reduced by your percentage of fault, and if that share reaches 50 percent or more, recovery is barred entirely. Insurers routinely attempt to assign partial blame to injured drivers to reduce what they pay out.
How to File a Grand Junction Car Accident Lawsuit
With a clear picture of liability and available coverage, the next step is understanding how the process works. Here is how it typically unfolds:
Investigation:
Your attorney gathers evidence, reviews police reports, interviews witnesses, and identifies every party that may share liability.
Damage Calculation:
Medical records, expert opinions, and financial documentation are used to build a complete picture of your losses, including future costs.
Demand Package:
A formal demand is sent to the relevant insurers outlining the facts, the liability, and the compensation being sought.
Negotiation:
Most cases resolve at this stage. If the insurer’s offer is fair, the case settles. If not, litigation begins.
Litigation:
When a fair outcome cannot be reached through negotiation, your attorney files a lawsuit and takes the case to court.
Timing matters as much as preparation. Under

, most personal injury claims must be filed within three years of the crash date, while wrongful death claims carry a two-year filing period. Missing either deadline permanently eliminates the right to recover. The sooner a
Grand Junction car accident lawyer
gets involved, the more time there is to build a complete factual record, engage the right experts, and put together a case that insurers take seriously.

faqs.question: Do I need a car accident lawyer after a crash in Grand Junction?

children.text: Not every crash requires an attorney, but any case involving injury, disputed fault, or significant damages benefits from legal guidance.

faqs.question: How long do I have to file a car accident claim in Colorado?

children.text: Colorado law gives most injury victims 3 years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit, though exceptions may apply.

faqs.question: Where do car accidents most often happen in Grand Junction?

children.text: High-frequency crash locations include I-70, North Avenue, Highway 50, and the Horizon Drive corridor through Mesa County.

faqs.question: Can I pursue compensation if I was partially at fault?

children.text: Yes, Colorado allows recovery as long as your share of fault is below 50 percent, though damages reduce proportionally.

faqs.question: Should I accept the insurance company's first settlement offer?

children.text: In most cases, no. Initial offers rarely reflect the full value of a claim, and a
Grand Junction car accident lawyer
can help you evaluate what you are actually owed.

faqs.question: How long does a Grand Junction car accident case usually take?

children.text: Straightforward cases may resolve in a few months; complex or litigated cases can take one to three years.
